Epileptogenic effect. Tonic-clonic seizures related to trazo- done therapy have been reported in 2 patients1,2 with no history of seizure disorders. 1. Bowdan ND. Seizure possibly caused by trazodone hydrochlo- ride. Am J Psychiatry 1983; 140: 642. 2. Lefkowitz D, et al. Seizures and trazodone therapy. Arch Gen Psychiatry 1985; 42: 523. Overdosage. Reviews have indicated that the incidence of se- rious toxicity from trazodone overdose alone was low compared with tricyclic antidepressant overdose.1-4 In a review covering 149 overdose cases,1 only 10 deaths had been reported and in only 1 case was trazodone the sole agent reported to be ingested; in this case autopsy revealed an acute myocardial infarction after the patient was stable. The remaining 9 patients also had histories of ingestion of unknown quantities of alcohol, benzodiazepines, or other sedative-hypnotics that may have contributed to their demise. In the surviving 139 pa- tients, 2 cases of respiratory arrest, 2 cases of right bundle branch block, and one case each of priapism, seizure, atrioventricular block, and T-wave inversion were reported.
